patronOf.en-US: The Child named Jesus on the eighth day
patronOf.pt-BR: O Menino recebe o nome de Jesus no oitavo dia

prayerExcerpt.en-US: May this year be one of fervor and of progress!
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Seja este ano um ano de fervor e de progresso!

meta.face: Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md: a young woman of about eighteen with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, lids lowered in a recollected gaze, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre under a white inner veil and a blue mantle drawn over the head. The Christ Child as in recurring-figures.md: a plump, ROUND baby face with full rosy cheeks, a high rounded forehead, a small button nose, large clear brown eyes, a small rosy mouth, soft short golden-brown curls, a plain gold halo, a newborn eight days old, eyes open and calm. St. Joseph as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about forty with a LONG OVAL face — a straight nose, gentle dark-brown eyes under level brows, a quiet mouth; full dark-brown curly hair to the nape and a short full dark-brown beard; green tunic and ochre-brown mantle. The elder: about sixty-five, a broad, ROUND face with full cheeks and a short, rounded grey beard, a short wide nose, kind crinkled dark eyes under bushy grey brows — clearly not Simeon's long face.
meta.basis: The scene follows Luke 2:21, which says only that the Child was circumcised and named Jesus on the eighth day; the card paints the naming, in a Bethlehem house, and keeps Our Lady, the Child and Joseph as on the Nativity and Epiphany cards. A book feast of the Pictorial Lives (1 January).
